changes.before: Build only main.cpp, with bonus.hpp present but without compiling/linking bonus.cpp. What fails?
changes.after: Compile separate source files and link their function calls to one definition.

before: A translation unit is a source file after preprocessing its includes. Compiling main.cpp can succeed because the compiler sees addBonus’s declaration; that alone does not supply its executable definition.

Build this example with g++ -std=c++23 main.cpp bonus.cpp -o example. Omitting bonus.cpp leaves the call without a supplied definition at link time. Giving the same ordinary function multiple definitions in separate files also violates the intended one-definition arrangement.
Expected output or behavior: 7. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Add a second caller in another source file while keeping the single bonus.cpp definition. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: A function declaration tells the compiler the function's name, inputs, and result type. bonus.hpp declares addBonus so main.cpp can compile a call to it.
A definition supplies the function's body. bonus.cpp contains the single definition of this ordinary function. Other source files can see its declaration without repeating that body.

Linking connects compiled parts into a program. With GCC, build both source files using g++ -std=c++23 main.cpp bonus.cpp -o example. Including a header does not automatically build another source file.
The program prints 7. The call in main.cpp reaches the definition in bonus.cpp, which adds three to four.

Compiling a call can succeed with only a declaration visible. Linking still needs the actual definition. Supplying this ordinary function's body in multiple source files also breaks the required single-definition arrangement.

before.question: Build only main.cpp, with bonus.hpp present but without compiling/linking bonus.cpp. What fails?
choices: The declaration is enough, so it prints 7.
Linking cannot find the supplied definition of addBonus.
before.explanation: The declaration lets the call compile. The missing definition leaves an unresolved reference during linking.

after.question: Build only main.cpp, with bonus.hpp present but without compiling and linking bonus.cpp. What fails?
choices: Nothing; the declaration is enough to print 7.
after.explanation: The declaration lets the call compile, but the missing compiled definition leaves the linker unable to complete the program.
